entries.effect: a caller gets NULL, and the CFError is left NULL - the port sets no error, because this signature's documentation names no domain or code for an unsupported algorithm. A caller diffing a TLS handshake or an ECDH suite gets NO SHARED SECRET, where a later release would get one: the value is a refusal, not a wrong secreta caller gets NULL, and the CFError names why: an NSError in NSOSStatusErrorDomain with errSecParam, the release's own code for a parameter it will not accept and the only one this signature's documentation leaves to say. An earlier version set no error at all, so a caller could not tell a refusal from an absence; the error is built in one place, CharonSecKeyFail, which the curve's refusals use as well. A key of the port's own kind exchanges over the curve and answers the 32 bytes a P-256 agreement makes - the X coordinate, or that digest of it when the algorithm's name ends in one - and the value is OpenSSL's own for the same two keys, byte for byte, measured on the host (tests/backports/host/seckeycurve). Nothing in the port sets that marker yet, because SecKeyCreateWithData is still absent, so no key of the release's keychain takes that path today.
entries.reason: the function arrived in iOS 10 and the release has NOTHING to exchange with, and that is measured rather than assumed: the armv7 shared cache of iOS 6.1.3 exports SecKeyRawSign, SecKeyRawVerify and no elliptic key agreement of any name, its only agreement being the finite-field SecDH family (SecDHComputeKey, SecDHGeneratePair), which is not a curve. It has an EC KEY TYPE - kSecAttrKeyTypeEC, SecItem.h:802-803, ios(4.0) - so the key a caller holds is real and the primitive underneath is not. An earlier version of this row read NO EC KEY TYPE AT ALL off kSecAttrKeyTypeECSECPrimeRandom, which is the 10.0 name for a different class; the two names are two lines apart in the same header. A key of THIS PACKAGE'S OWN KIND - one that carries its own private scalar, beside the kSecValueData SecKeyCreateWithData would have left, and that the release's keychain therefore does not hold - is answered by the curve in Security/SecKeyElliptic10.m instead, and the two are told apart by that one attribute. The public symbol is this one, once, for both: two objects of one library defining one name is a link error, and the 6.1.3 gate answered with four of them.
